learning_outcomes.text: Has basic knowledge of the operation of modern measuring instruments, including in automation systems.
Is familiar with the current state and latest development trends in electrical measurement.
Can analyze and design measurement systems for electrical quantities and selected non-electrical quantities, and perform measurements and process results, including assessing measurement uncertainty.

Is aware of the importance and understands the non-technical aspects and consequences of an electrical engineer's activities, including their impact on environmental safety and the associated responsibility for decisions made.

syllabus_topics: Laboratory classes on lecture topics: - measurement systems in multiphase networks - isolators and instrument transformers - digital measuring instruments and digital measurement techniques - application of measurement techniques for measuring non-electrical quantities with sensors

Lecture topics: 1. Separation issues: instrument transformers and isolators. The need for separation of measurement systems, instrument transformers, modern isolators - operating principle and metrological properties. 2. Measurement of time, frequency, phase with particular emphasis on digital techniques. Application of oscilloscope measurement techniques for time measurement, technical methods in frequency measurements, digital instruments for time and frequency measurement. 3. Digital voltmeters. Integrating converters. 4. Digital voltmeters. Compensation converters, the idea of D/A converters. 5. Digital voltmeters. Direct comparison and sigma-delta converters, propagation converters. 6. Measurement uncertainties with digital instruments. Reading user documentation of digital instruments, methods for calculating measurement uncertainty for digital instruments. 7. Analog measurement systems. Measurement channel with amplitude modulation, analog methods of transmitting measurement data. Protection of electronic measuring equipment. 8. Measurement of selected non-electrical quantities by electrical methods. Measurement of relative length changes using strain gauges, inductive sensors, capacitive sensors. 9. Links between metrology and vocational subjects, summary of lecture topics. Prospects for the development of electrical metrology, distributed measurement systems and digital technology, information about the exam.
assessment_rules: Lectures: Students participate in classes, learning subsequent teaching content according to the course syllabus. Students should ask questions and clarify doubts on an ongoing basis. Audiovisual recording of the lecture requires the instructor's consent. Laboratory classes: Students perform laboratory exercises according to the materials provided by the instructor. The student is obliged to prepare for the performed exercise, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Passing the classes is based on presenting the solution to the posed problem. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
